messages:
Maya Chen: hitting a weird edge in the async python client — when an HTTP 422 comes back inside an `async with client.request(...)` block the exception I get has only a short message, no status, no body. I think we swallow something in the context manager.
Samir Patel: ugh that sounds bad. can you paste a tiny repro? which client version?
Maya Chen: using 0.9.3 with aiohttp transport. repro:
```py
async with Client() as c:
    await c.post('/v1/embed', json={"text": "bad"})
# raises SDKError('validation failed') but no .status_code or .raw_body
```
Samir Patel: ok lemme try locally. quick Q: is the underlying aiohttp response closed by the context manager before we build the exception?
Ivy Park: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/issues/4567 — we've seen this pattern. async context manager currently closes/consumes the response stream to avoid leaks, but we don't stash the raw bytes if an error path is hit. we should keep a small raw_body bytes fallback, plus request_id header.
Maya Chen: yes exactly — I tried catching, but by the time exception surfaces the body is gone. also observed non-utf8 payloads (bob/emoji) cause decode errors if we try to decode naively.
Samir Patel: quick patch idea: when status >= 400, read resp.content.read() into bytes, attach as exception.raw_body (bytes) and exception.text as best-effort decode('utf-8', 'replace'). also include status_code and headers. typings: expose raw_body: Optional[bytes] in Exception dataclass.
Ivy Park: agree. API shape suggestion:
```py
class APIError(Exception):
    message: str
    status_code: Optional[int]
    headers: Dict[str,str]
    raw_body: Optional[bytes]  # preserved for diagnostics
    text: Optional[str]  # decoded with 'replace'
    request_id: Optional[str]
```
Maya Chen: that would make on-call debugging way easier. can we make this work for both sync and async transports without duplicate logic?
Samir Patel: yes — unify in http/response_utils.py: `capture_error_payload(resp)` used by both transports. small perf cost only on error paths.
ci-bot: Build #3721 passed on branch: fix/error-exc-payload (tests: +3 -0) :white_check_mark:
Ivy Park: add a typed APIError in `sdk.errors` so mypy users can `except APIError as e: assert isinstance(e.raw_body, (bytes, type(None)))`. also add a short helper `e.json()` that tries `json.loads(e.raw_body)` and returns None on failure.
Maya Chen: one more DX ask — include the original request object reference (or at least method+url+body snippet) in the exception for debugging. redwood-telemetry can then link payloads.
Samir Patel: ok will open a PR that: preserves raw_body (bytes), status_code, headers, request_id, and method/url snippet; adds `APIError.json()` helper; updates typings. will also add a changelog entry about compatibility. link when ready.
Maya Chen: awesome. also file a follow-up to document how to handle large bodies (we should cap preserved bytes to 64KB) — no need to stash multi-meg responses.
Ivy Park: agree on cap and add `raw_body_truncated` bool. please include tests for non-utf8 decoding and for `async with` codepaths.
Samir Patel: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/4892 — cc: @Maya Chen for quick review, CI bumped.
Maya Chen: reviewing now, thanks. :raised_hands:
ci-bot: Tests for PR #4892 are running...
Samir Patel: thanks everyone. after this lands we should update examples in the quickstart to show how to extract `.status_code` and `.raw_body` on errors so customers don't get surprised.
Maya Chen: agreed — reducing onboarding friction. once merged I'll re-run reproducer and confirm error payload present in my stack traces.
Ivy Park: note for release notes: call out async parity, error typing, preserved raw bytes, and 64KB cap.
ci-bot: PR #4892 merged into main (commit 9f3b2a).
Maya Chen: verified fixed on my repro — thanks! :tada:
